policy: No third-party proprietary code copied. MIT repositories are references/candidates; if code is copied later, preserve license notice.

references.title: Reform Collective: A New Website, Designed to Be Seen — Codrops
references.transfer: Clarity, performance and structure first; expressive CSS scenes can be isolated instead of defining every page.
references.reject: Do not reproduce its studio skin, scroll controller or 3D block effect as site-wide identity.

references.title: Spain Collection: Evolving a Luxury Website into a Digital Ecosystem — Codrops
references.transfer: Editorial art direction, generous breathing room, explicit content architecture and memorable but subtle interaction; distinct page families can share one system.
references.reject: Do not import luxury-travel visual language, large photo dependency or modal catalog mechanics where they do not serve author-site tasks.

references.title: The Exat Microsite: Pushing a Typography Showcase to New Creative Extremes — Codrops
references.transfer: Typography can be the interface; alternate calm reading sections with one expressive scene, and let scroll structure pacing rather than trigger decoration everywhere.
references.reject: Do not imitate type-specimen effects or make continuous motion carry information.

references.title: Setting the Stage: Christian Fleming — Codrops
references.transfer: Prototype against hostile long titles and mobile early; hierarchy can come from type weight, placement and negative space rather than more components.
references.reject: Do not transfer the theatrical skin or central photo staging literally.

references.title: Turning Music Into Motion: 24/7 Artists — Codrops
references.transfer: Storyboard a long page as a sequence of states and transitions before coding; prioritize bold effects that are achievable and understood by the implementation team.
references.reject: Do not transfer mouse trails, music visualizer aesthetics or full-screen spectacle to an author site.
